text: You signed something with a lot of pages and did not read most of them.
You slept in your own place for the first time and it was too quiet.
You learned to cook one thing properly and made it constantly.
The shower ran cold for six weeks before anyone came.
The car made a noise. You turned the radio up.
You passed a test you had failed before and told nobody about the first attempt.
Everyone you knew got married in the same eighteen months.
It became the decade of funerals rather than weddings.
You joined a gym in January and stopped going in March.
You kept it up all year, which surprised everyone including you.
You changed how you eat and felt righteous for about a month.
You drank less this year and noticed the difference more than you expected.
You went somewhere warm and came back with a plan you never acted on.
The holiday rained for nine days and became a story instead.
You saw a band you loved at nineteen and half the crowd was your age.
A book got under your skin and stayed there for months.
You cried at a film and blamed being tired.
You replaced something that still worked and felt vaguely guilty.
The dentist used the word 'eventually' and left it there.
Your prescription changed and the world sharpened for a week.
You had the conversation with the neighbours. It half worked.
You fixed something yourself and it held, mostly.
You grew something on purpose and it survived.
You lost something small and looked for it far longer than it was worth.
A stranger did you a small kindness you still think about.
Someone was rude to you for no reason and it stuck for days.
You apologised for something a year late and meant it.
You kept a grudge going past the point where anyone remembered why.
You went to a reunion and everyone had become themselves, more so.
You said something out loud for the first time and it was easier after.
There was a stretch of months you would rather not go over again.
You gave some time to something that had nothing to do with you.
You voted, and spent the evening refreshing the same page.
The news was heavy for months and you started avoiding it.
Something new arrived that everyone insisted would change everything.
You explained something obsolete to someone younger and felt every year of it.
You set a number to save to and got about two-thirds of the way.
You got more money and your spending quietly rose to meet it.
You lent money you privately wrote off as you handed it over.
You finally sorted the paperwork you had been ignoring for years.
You did the paperwork at the last possible moment, as always.
You wondered, seriously, whether this was the life you had chosen.
You caught yourself being happy and did not immediately look for the catch.
Your body changed shape and stopped changing back.
You found the first grey and left it alone.
A single late night now costs two days.
You made a genuinely new friend, which gets harder every year.
Someone younger asked your advice and you were careful with it.
Someone you assumed would always be there was not.
The house got quieter and you kept the radio on more.
The young ones visited and left the place wrecked and better.
You took the same walk and it took longer.
You wrote to someone properly, on paper, for the first time in decades.
You started sorting things out so nobody else would have to.
You told a story you have told before, and they let you.
Another year. You noticed that, this time.
